classification: law by finite counterexample, Lean kernel checked
statement: Pairwise intersection does not imply joint intersection for arbitrary finite nonconvex subsets (combs).
domain: Finite carrier {0,1,2}; A={0,1}, B={1,2}, C={0,2}. Witnesses AB=1, AC=0, BC=2; ABC empty.
hypotheses: No convexity/interval assumption. C has a hole. Does not refute the interval-only T38.
negative: Reject promoting pairwise compatibility of these combs to a global witness.
existing: Classical Helly theory needs convexity; finite intervals on a line are 2-Helly. The elementary nonconvex counterexample is not a new discovery.
adds: Exact finite subset witness and compiled Lean certificate tied to Obligations candidate bytes; no new form or wire encoding.
status: finite witness checked; no generalized theorem
